And it's actually the third paragraph that I'm directing your attention to. You speak of the corpses that go into many morgues in the area of Sarajevo, Banja Luka or in Tuzla, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know if it's limited to just those three areas where the morgues are or were there more than morgues -- more morgues than that, sorry?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not that familiar with the morgues, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I have to go back on page 11 and ask you because I wasn't clear on your answer when you discussed the 7.000 body-bags that were stored in the Tuzla morgues. It appears on the first paragraph, fifth line, do you see it?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: My question to you, sir, is: Where did you obtain that information?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the ICMP. It says, according to the PIP, Podrinje Identification Projects. It says 7.000 body-bags. According to the ICMP, the number of missing persons from Srebrenica is 7.789.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But let me ask you this: Did you ask any of the office of the Prosecution anthropologists, pathologists, archeologists as to how many body-bags there were that were stored in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is part of it. I did not ask because this is part -- this is the answer, 7.000 body-bags.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's what the OTP pathologists suggest as well? Is that your --

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not talk to them about that but there is close cooperation between the PIP and the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, the very next paragraph you talk about the most reliable source on the exhumed and identified bodies, persons, is with, no doubt, the ICMP, correct?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that relative to the reports as a source by the archeologists, pathologists and anthropologists that have worked for the office of the Prosecution? Are you making a distinction that they are not as reliable as the ICMP?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course not.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Why would you say that that they are the most reliable source?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are talking about different dimensions. The anthropologists, et cetera, they look at individual cases, try to explain the age, the cause of death and so on but we want, we are interested in the large databases of as many individuals as possible, and the anthropologists usually do not collect such large databases whereas ICMP has done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And then you use this source to determine whether or not it's higher than the ICRC base, correct?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It says it in the very next sentence actually.

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Equal to or higher than -- yeah. We used this source to check whether the number of known deaths is equal to or higher than the ICRC base total of 2.054 deaths.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So you used your two information sources to cross-reference with one another on this point, corrects?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you say that it's found or discussed elsewhere. Where would I find the results of this exercise?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: We looked at -- this is in the whole report. We looked at the identified exhumed bodies and compared 2.500 and something and compare that with a list of missing persons and the identified persons, missing persons, also in the ICRC list.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So it's not identified elsewhere in the report, it's identified throughout your report, is that maybe a different way of saying it?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I couldn't find the section so --

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, no, it's okay. Now just moving quickly in the interests of time if we can, the next paragraph after that which would be the fourth paragraph of your report, you talk about traditional methods of identification; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you say five to 8 per cent of the exhumed bodies; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You're not a forensic pathologist, archeologist or anthropologist; correct?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But are you, sir, a forensic demographer?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No I wouldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What is forensic demography?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no such a thing but I think some people would perhaps call me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, in your article of 2007 you talk about forensic demography and the role that it plays in estimating war casualties.

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that on page 3 or page 2 of that actual article on the introduction?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You remember that?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What is it? What is forensic demography and why do people call you that?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we are concerned with exhumed bodies, for example, in a crisis situation. So that's why we have forensic criminology and law and medicine, so that is a natural parallel.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I understand about the law and all the other areas you discuss but in demography how would you describe it? How is it different from what you've been doing, forensic demography, as opposed to what I consider just scientific, statistical demography?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the object of the study that's of interest here. The methods are exactly the same but the objects, missing and dead people, exhumations especially, that is why it could be called forensic demography.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me, sir, as I think you will, that forensic demography will give us a more precise result if our objective was to determine what the war casualties were in a given situation or a period?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if forensic demography develops methods that are unique for that, then it can contribute to provide better estimates.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And am I correct, sir, that your report is not one that would be considered as forensic demographic report but it is simply a statistical demographic report if one were to compare the two?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not up to me to give names to this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's your report. I suggest to you that it is not a forensic demographic report at all and it doesn't go into the details at all of the war casualties and doesn't have a breakdown of any of the classifications that you yourself are -- identify as being important for determining conflict situations and manner and cause of death; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct but that is your definition of forensic demography.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's why I asked for your definition, sir. What are those methodologies that you, as a forensic demographer as people from time to time call you, would utilise that would render more precise information on war consequences or war casualties?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example, the utilisation of DNA analysis to identify exhumed bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you think, doctor, that that would go more for identification or to cause of death?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: More for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What about for cause of death, whether it was involved as you related it a battle, battlefield or combat or non-combat-related death? What's the methodology that one would use in order to determine that?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then you would need different data sets.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Such as?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Say a military source of deaths in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What other methodology would you utilise?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be the basic -- If you have a battle and you want to decide how many people died in the battle, then you need that kind of data source, some estimates of who died in the battle.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That would be a source, that military information, what other sources do you think would be able to help us to determine that?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cause of death statistics might be useful.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Eyewitness testimony, right?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: M'hm, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What about the methodology? I know you mentioned that as a source and sometimes from time to time people do mix source with methodology. Is the methodology system the same if you're doing forensic demography that you would utilise a match or linking methodology, or as you suggested a sample methodology which, I suggest, is far less precise?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course a source is not the same as methodology.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So what's the methodology that would be utilised? How is it called?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here we use simple matching methodology to check data and matching data from different sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so I understand, even in forensic demography we would still utilise the same methodology known as match or linking methodology, correct?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: As one of the methods, yes. There could be other methods also.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Name some for me.

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you're interested in cause of death then you need to utilise cause of death data. There is one part of demography that is concerned with cause of death. Another one is not -- only concerned with the total number of deaths or life expectancy or death rates.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, since we are talking, we only have a few minutes, if I can just end maybe with this, Mr. President -- may I ask one more question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned today on page 43 --

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, on which report? My report doesn't have that many pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: On the testimony today on page 43 of your testimony, you state, sir, on page 43 and 44 actually, commencing on lines 24 through 25: "So DNA analysis and identification and comparison with victims has to be done before we can say for sure how many people were killed." Do you remember saying that, sir?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I want to emphasise the word "for sure". Are you saying that before we can make a determination as to how many people were killed, based upon a reasonable degree of scientific certainty, we would have to have, in order to be determined beyond a reasonable doubt, such DNA analysis and identification for comparison with victims, correct?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection calls for a legal conclusion; "beyond a reasonable doubt".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What's your remark, comments on that, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I would just like to have the doctor expand on "for sure". He's obviously listed in his report other legal conclusions that the Prosecutor did not object to and offered into evidence, as we've discussed, and the doctor was kind enough to tell us that he'd like them to be removed, such as killing. And all I want, and I was just trying to assist, is what he meant by "for sure", so I could restate the question if the Court permits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But I disagree with the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's the case of rephrasing the question, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Doctor, what did you mean when you said, "Before we can say for sure how many people were killed"?

utterances.speaker: HELGE BRUNBORG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do not remember the context but what I think I meant is that if you just have the missing -- a list of missing persons and if you don't know they are dead there is no evidence of death, you cannot be sure that they are all dead. And whether it's DNA analysis or some other kind of analysis, pathologists or forensic whatever, then we need to know that before we can say whether people are dead or not. These lists are called lists of missing and dead persons. We have now so far been able to estimate more than one-third of the missing persons but two-thirds remained. And the evidence is very strong that they are also dead, but as I said we cannot know for sure until we have identified all of them and they have been linked to persons reported as missing and who were living before the conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
